title: Why the Moon Causes Tides
hook: The Moon doesn't lift the oceans so much as stretch them. Tides come from the difference in its pull across the width of the Earth.
key_points: The Moon pulls Earth's near side harder than its far side.
This difference stretches the oceans into two bulges — near and far.
Earth rotating through both bulges gives roughly two high tides a day.
The Sun adds in: aligned gives big spring tides, right-angled gives small neap tides.
content_html: It's tempting to picture the Moon simply lifting the sea toward it, but the real story is about a difference. Gravity weakens with distance, so the Moon pulls the side of Earth facing it a bit harder than it pulls the planet's center, and it pulls the far side weaker still. That gradient stretches the oceans into two bulges — one toward the Moon, one away from it.
extra_html: As the Earth rotates each day, any coastline passes through both bulges, which is why most places see roughly two high tides and two low tides daily. The Sun pulls too, with a smaller effect because it's so far away. When Sun and Moon line up, their pulls combine into large spring tides; when they sit at right angles, the pulls partly cancel into gentler neap tides. Wikipedia details this interplay and the local geography that shapes real tides.

flashcards.prompt: Why are there two tidal bulges, not just one?
flashcards.back_html: The Moon pulls the near side harder and the far side less than Earth's center, stretching the oceans into bulges on both sides.

choices.text: The difference in the Moon's gravity across the width of the Earth
The Moon's heat warming and expanding the seas
The Earth's own spin throwing water outward

flashcards.explanation_html: Tides arise because the Moon pulls the near side of Earth more than the far side. That difference stretches the oceans into two bulges.

flashcards.prompt: When do the largest (spring) tides occur?

choices.text: When the Sun and Moon line up so their pulls add together
When the Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other
Only during the coldest months of the year

flashcards.explanation_html: Spring tides happen when Sun and Moon align and their tidal pulls combine. At right angles they partly cancel, giving smaller neap tides.
